info.title: Ticketing API
info.description: Implemented Catalog, Orders and Inventory HTTP contracts. Public operations authenticate a customer or admin. AWS API Gateway validates JWTs and overwrites trusted identity headers; local mode accepts only the documented synthetic bearer identities. Internal Inventory routes rely on private network access and are not API Gateway routes. 202 means durable acceptance, not a guaranteed reservation or completed sale. No payments, manual cancellation, refunds or transitions out of SOLD/COMPLIMENTARY are implemented. The 16 KiB body limit currently maps to 400 in Catalog/Orders and 413 in Inventory. See docs/contracts.md for source mapping, limitations and PDF traceability.

get.description: Returns numbered entries in ascending numeric order. Expired holders encountered on the page are released as whole reservations before rereading. Availability remains authoritative only when a reservation transaction succeeds.

200.description: Read an atomic snapshot of all 16 counter shards

get.description: Reads metadata plus 16 counter shards in one DynamoDB transaction. capacity equals the sum of the five state counters. A primary-table freshness check returns 503 INVENTORY_STALE when an unreleased reservation is more than five seconds overdue. This five-second policy is an implementation choice, not a PDF-specified SLA.

post.description: Requires exact admin group, beneficiaryId and a nonblank reason. Persists a complimentary request for the beneficiary. COMPLIMENTARY is final, consumes capacity, and does not count as a sale. 202 does not guarantee capacity. The beneficiary owns subsequent GET access; an admin has no blanket read bypass.

servers.description: Private Compose network; used by Orders

put.summary: Reserve all selected entries or persist a rejection
put.description: No Idempotency-Key header: orderId is the immutable idempotency key. 200 can be AVAILABLE with TICKETS_UNAVAILABLE or RESERVATION_EXPIRED. A successful PURCHASE writes its expiry timer outbox in the same Inventory transaction. Access is restricted by private network policy, not bearer authentication.

get.summary: Read and materialize logical expiry for one reservation

servers.description: Private Compose network; used by Orders

post.summary: Private recovery operation; the public normal path is asynchronous
post.description: Private equivalent of processing ConfirmPurchase. Same customer and commandId must be preserved. RESERVED -> PENDING_CONFIRMATION -> SOLD uses two conditional transactions and one unchanged deadline. A held reservation observed at its deadline can return the newly expired snapshot; replay of an already expired reservation returns 409. SOLD stays final.

bearerAuth.description: JWT at AWS ingress. Local profile with AUTH_MODE=local uses local-customer-1, local-customer-2 or local-admin as synthetic bearer values; these are not JWTs.

startsAt.description: Must be strictly later than the server clock at creation.

resolution.description: Empty before authority is known; NONE for an active/final allocation; TICKETS_UNAVAILABLE or RESERVATION_EXPIRED for a resolved rejection/release.

expiresAt.description: Original requestedAt plus 600 seconds. Retries, confirmations and reconciliation preserve this timestamp.

Order.description: status describes this order assignment. AVAILABLE with RESERVING, REJECTED or EXPIRED does not assert that its historical requested tickets are currently free. requestedTicketIds is history; activeTicketIds is the current assignment.

ReserveReservation.description: Private command. Path orderId is authoritative; a supplied body orderId is ignored. expiresAt must be after requestedAt and no more than 600 seconds later. requestedAt may not exceed Inventory clock by more than two seconds. A past deadline creates a durable rejection. Replays must preserve the normalized payload and selected ticket ordering.
